metadata.title: A new type of Ramsey-Turán problems
metadata.authors: H. Li, V. Nikiforov, R.H. Schelp

nodes.name: 2-coloring of a graph
nodes.statement: A $2$-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition $E(G) = E(R) \cup E(B)$, where $R$ and $B$ are subgraphs of $G$ with $V(R) = V(B) = V(G)$.

nodes.name: Graph notation: $ec(G)$ and $oc(G)$
nodes.statement: $ec(G)$ and $oc(G)$ denote the lengths of the longest even and odd cycles in $G$. $\Gamma_G(u)$ is the neighborhood, $d_G(u) = |\Gamma_G(u)|$, and $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree.

nodes.name: Theorem A (Bondy)
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a graph of order $n$ with $\delta(G) > n/2$, then $G$ contains $C_k$ for all $k \in [3, n]$.

nodes.name: Theorem B (Bollobás)
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a graph of order $n$ with $e(G) > n^2/4$, then $G$ contains $C_k$ for all $k \in [3, \lceil n/2 \rceil]$.

nodes.name: Theorem C (Häggkvist)
nodes.statement: Let $k \geq 2$ and let $G$ be a nonbipartite, $2$-connected graph of sufficiently large order $n$. If $\delta(G) > \frac{2}{2k+1} n$, then $G$ contains a $C_{2k-1}$.

nodes.name: Theorem D (Gould, Haxell, Scott)
nodes.statement: For all $c > 0$, there exists $K = K(c)$ such that if $G$ has order $n > K$ with $\delta(G) \geq cn$, then $C_k \subset G$ for all even $k \in [4, ec(G) - K]$ and all odd $k \in [K, oc(G) - K]$.
conclusions: $C_k \subset G$ for all even $k \in [4, ec(G)-K]$ and odd $k \in [K, oc(G)-K]$

nodes.name: Theorem E (Erdős, Gallai)
nodes.statement: Let $k \geq 1$. If $e(G) > k|G|/2$, then $G$ contains a path and a cycle of length at least $k+1$.
conclusions: $G$ contains a path of length $\geq k+1$
$G$ contains a cycle of length $\geq k+1$

nodes.name: Nikiforov-Schelp Ramsey-Turán result
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph of sufficiently large order $2n-1$ with $\delta(G) \geq (2 - 10^{-6}) n$. If $E(G) = E(R) \cup E(B)$ is a $2$-coloring, then $C_k \subset R$ for all $k \in [3, n]$ or $C_k \subset B$ for all $k \in [3, n]$.
conclusions: $C_k \subset R$ for all $k \in [3, n]$, or $C_k \subset B$ for all $k \in [3, n]$

nodes.name: Main conjecture (Conjecture 1)
nodes.statement: Let $n \geq 4$ and let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ with $\delta(G) > 3n/4$. If $E(G) = E(R) \cup E(B)$ is a $2$-coloring, then $C_k \subset R$ or $C_k \subset B$ for all $k \in [4, \lceil n/2 \rceil]$.
conclusions: $C_k \subset R$ or $C_k \subset B$ for all $k \in [4, \lceil n/2 \rceil]$

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (partial solution to Conjecture 1)
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and $G$ be a graph of sufficiently large order $n$ with $\delta(G) > 3n/4$. If $E(G) = E(R) \cup E(B)$ is a $2$-coloring, then $C_k \subset R$ or $C_k \subset B$ for all $k \in [4, \lfloor (1/8 - \varepsilon) n \rfloor]$.
conclusions: $C_k \subset R$ or $C_k \subset B$ for all $k \in [4, \lfloor (1/8 - \varepsilon) n \rfloor]$

nodes.name: Main assumption (no monochromatic $k$-cycle)
nodes.statement: For contradiction: $n$ is sufficiently large and there is no monochromatic $k$-cycle for some $k \in [4, \lfloor (1/8 - \varepsilon) n \rfloor]$.

nodes.name: Claim 1: $R$ and $B$ are nonbipartite
nodes.statement: Both graphs $R$ and $B$ are nonbipartite.

nodes.name: Claim 3: minimum-degree bounds
nodes.statement: $\delta(R) > 2\varepsilon n$ and $\delta(B) > 2\varepsilon n$.

nodes.name: Claim 4: at least one of $R$, $B$ is $2$-connected
nodes.statement: At least one of the graphs $R$ or $B$ is $2$-connected.

nodes.name: Claim 5: large $\Delta(B)$ forces $C_{2k+1} \subset B$
nodes.section: Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles
nodes.statement: If $\Delta(B) \geq n/2 + 4k$, then $B$ contains a $C_{2k+1}$.

nodes.name: Claim 6: long cycles in $R$
nodes.statement: $ec(R) > n/8 - 2k$ and $oc(R) > n/8 - 2k$.

nodes.name: Conjecture 2 (concluding)
nodes.statement: Let $0 < c < 1$ and $G$ be a graph of sufficiently large order $n$. If $\delta(G) > cn$, then for every $2$-coloring of $E(G)$, there is a monochromatic $C_k$ for some $k \geq cn$.
conclusions: there is a monochromatic $C_k$ for some $k \geq cn$

nodes.name: Tight extremal coloring of $K_{2p,2p}$ + red $K_{p,p}$
nodes.statement: Let $n = 4p$, color edges of $K_{2p,2p}$ blue, insert a red $K_{p,p}$ in each vertex class. The resulting $G$ has $\delta(G) = 3n/4$ and the coloring produces no monochromatic odd cycle.

nodes.name: Blow-up of red/blue $5$-cycle on $K_5$
nodes.statement: Splitting $K_5$ into a blue and a red $5$-cycle and blowing up the coloring yields a graph $G$ with $\delta(G) = 4n/5$ that has no monochromatic triangle.

nodes.name: Many extremal colorings of complete $4$-partite graph
nodes.statement: For $G = K_{p,p,p,p}$ with $n = 4p$, color $U_1\!-\!U_2$ and $U_3\!-\!U_4$ blue, $U_1\!-\!U_3$ and $U_2\!-\!U_4$ red, and $U_1\!-\!U_4$, $U_2\!-\!U_3$ arbitrarily; this yields $2^{n^2/8 - O(n \log n)}$ non-isomorphic monochromatic-odd-cycle-free colorings.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1
nodes.statement: Suppose $B$ bipartite with classes $U, W$, $|U| \geq |W|$. For $u \in U$, $d_{R[U]}(u) > 3n/4 - n + |U| \geq |U|/2$, so by Theorem A, $R[U]$ has $C_k$ for all $k \in [3, |U|]$, contradicting the main assumption.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 2
nodes.statement: If $e(R) \leq n^2/8$, then $e(B) \geq \delta n/2 - e(R) > n^2/4$, and Theorem B yields $C_k \subset B$ for all $k \in [3, \lceil n/2 \rceil]$ — contradicting the main assumption.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3
nodes.statement: Assume $d_R(u) \leq 2\varepsilon n$. Bound $e(R[U]) + e(B[U])$ above and below, using Theorem B and Theorem E to control $e(R[U])$ and forbid long $B[U]$-paths; conclude $|U| < (3/4 - 2\varepsilon) n$, contradicting $d_B(u) > (3/4 - 2\varepsilon) n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 4
nodes.statement: Suppose both $R$ and $B$ are at most $1$-connected. Removing $S = \{u, v\}$ disconnects both, partitioning $W = V \setminus S$ into $V_1, V_2, V_3, V_4$ with no $G$-edges between $V_1$–$V_4$ or $V_2$–$V_3$; degree sum yields $3n - 3|S| - 4 \geq 4(\delta(G) - |S|) > 3n - 4|S|$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5
nodes.section: Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles
nodes.statement: Pick $u$ with $d_B(u) = \Delta(B)$, set $U = \Gamma_B(u)$. If $B[U]$ has a path of order $2k$ then $C_{2k+1} \subset B$. Otherwise edge counts on $R[U]$ via Theorem B and on $B[U]$ force $|U| < n/2 + 4k$, contradicting $d_B(u) \geq n/2 + 4k$.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 6
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem C to obtain a $(2r-1)$-cycle $C'$ in $R$ with $r = \lceil 1/2\varepsilon \rceil$. Remove $V(C')$; Theorem E yields a long cycle $C''$. Use $2$-connectivity to glue $C'$ and $C''$ via two disjoint paths, producing both an odd and an even cycle of length $> n/8 - 2r$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.section: Proof of Theorem 1; Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles; Existence of all cycles
nodes.statement: By contradiction via the main assumption. Establish Claims 1–4 (structural properties of $R, B$), then Claim 5 plus Theorem C handles odd $C_{2k+1}$ for $k \geq 4$; a separate three-case argument handles $C_5$. Finally Claim 6 plus Theorem D yields all even and odd $k$-cycles in $R$ for $k \in [4, n/8 - L]$.

nodes.name: Establish Claims 1–4 (structural setup)
nodes.statement: From the main assumption, derive that $R, B$ are nonbipartite (Claim 1), $e(R), e(B) > n^2/8$ (Claim 2), $\delta(R), \delta(B) > 2\varepsilon n$ (Claim 3), and at least one of $R, B$ is $2$-connected (Claim 4).

nodes.name: Reduce to $\Delta(B) < n/2 + 4k$
nodes.section: Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles
nodes.statement: By Claim 5, if $\Delta(B) \geq n/2 + 4k$ we already have $C_{2k+1} \subset B$. Hence assume $\Delta(B) < n/2 + 4k$, giving $\delta(R) > n/4 - 4k$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem C for $C_{2k-1} \subset R$ with $k \geq 4$
nodes.section: Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles
nodes.statement: Since $R$ is $2$-connected, nonbipartite, with $\delta(R) > n/4 - 4k > 2n/(2k+1)$ for $k \geq 4$, Theorem C yields $C_{2k-1} \subset R$.

nodes.name: Three-case argument for $C_5$
nodes.section: Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles
nodes.statement: Assume no monochromatic $C_5$ and split into cases: (i) $R$ triangle-free, (ii) $R$ has triangles but no two share an edge, (iii) $R$ has two triangles sharing an edge; each case derives a contradiction via degree/disjointness counting.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem D using Claim 6 to get all $k$-cycles in $R$
nodes.statement: Setting $K = K(2\varepsilon)$ and $L = 2\lceil 1/2\varepsilon \rceil + K$, Theorem D combined with Claim 6 gives $C_k \subset R$ for all even $k \in [4, n/8 - L]$ and all odd $k \in [K, n/8 - L]$, contradicting the main assumption.

nodes.name: Case (i): $R$ triangle-free
nodes.section: Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles
nodes.statement: Theorem C gives an induced $7$-cycle $C$ in $R$. The complementary $7$-cycle $C'$ in $B$ on the same vertices, together with $\sum_{i=1}^7 d_B(v_i) > 13n/4$, yields a vertex joined in $B$ to $4$ vertices of $C'$, producing $C_5 \subset B$, contradiction.

nodes.name: Case (ii): triangles share no edge
nodes.section: Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles
nodes.statement: For triangle vertices $v_1, v_2, v_3$ with neighborhoods $U_i$, no $C_5$ forces $|U_i \cap U_j| = 1$. Show six sets $U_i', W_i$ are pairwise disjoint, giving $n \geq 6(n/4 - 18)$, contradiction for large $n$.

nodes.name: Case (iii): two triangles share an edge
nodes.section: Existence of monochromatic short odd cycles
nodes.statement: For triangles $v_1 v_2 v_4$, $v_2 v_3 v_4$, similar disjointness analysis yields $n \geq 3(n/4 - 19) + 3(n/4 - 18)$, contradicting $n$ large.

nodes.name: Lower bound $d_B(u)$ when $d_R(u)$ is small
nodes.statement: $d_B(u) = \delta(G) - d_R(u) > (3/4 - 2\varepsilon) n$.

nodes.name: Note on monochromatic triangles under $\delta > 3n/4$
nodes.statement: Under the premises of Conjecture 1, a monochromatic triangle is not guaranteed: blowing up the red/blue $5$-cycle decomposition of $K_5$ yields $\delta(G) = 4n/5$ with no monochromatic triangle (Sós 1969).
